You know your subject and you want to teach it online. What you do not want is
to learn web design, or to argue with a learning platform's editor about where a
picture goes.

This template turns plain text files into a complete course website: chapters
with a sidebar, search, self-check quizzes, lecture slides, a dark mode, and a
layout that works on a phone. Colours, typeface and logo placement already
follow the Universitätsmedizin Göttingen corporate design, so nobody has to
decide them again.

**This course is built with the template it teaches.** Every feature you read
about is in use on the page in front of you, and the files behind these pages
are the worked examples. When a chapter says "see how it is done", open the
matching `.qmd` file and look.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "The workflow of this course. You repeat the first three steps as often as you like; publishing is a routine of three clicks."
%%| fig-alt: "Four boxes in a row, joined by arrows: 1 Write chapters as text files, 2 Render in RStudio, 3 Check the pages in the docs folder, 4 Publish on GitHub or GitLab Pages."
flowchart LR
    A["Step 1<br/>Write chapters<br/>as text files"] --> B["Step 2<br/>Render with one<br/>click in RStudio"]
    B --> C["Step 3<br/>Check the pages<br/>in the docs folder"]
    C --> D["Step 4<br/>Publish on GitHub<br/>or GitLab Pages"]

    classDef mine fill:#203151,stroke:#203151,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef theirs fill:#f1a400,stroke:#f1a400,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000
    class A,B,C mine
    class D theirs
```

::: {.objectives}
**By the end of this course you will be able to**

- Install the software and build your first course website from the template
- Plan a course as chapters with objectives that can be checked
- Write content: headings, images, tables, callouts, diagrams, references
- Add self-check questions that give learners immediate feedback
- Prepare lecture slides and run a checklist before release
- Publish the course on GitHub or GitLab Pages, and update it later
:::

## How this course works

There are eight short chapters, in four groups. Each has the same shape:
objectives at the top, explanation with examples, and questions at the end. Plan
on about **three to four hours** in total, and take them in order the first time.
You can stop after any chapter and come back.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-course-map
%%| fig-cap: "Route through the material. Take the chapters in order the first time."
%%| fig-alt: "Eight chapters in four groups. Get going: 1 Set up and first render, 2 Plan and structure. Write: 3 Write text, 4 Images, tables, diagrams and references, 5 Quizzes. Slides and release: 6 Slides, 7 Check before release, 8 Publish."
flowchart LR
    subgraph G1["Get going"]
        A["1 Set up<br/>and first render"] --> B["2 Plan and<br/>structure"]
    end
    subgraph G2["Write"]
        C["3 Write<br/>text"] --> D["4 Images, tables,<br/>references"] --> E["5 Quizzes"]
    end
    subgraph G3["Slides and release"]
        F["6 Slides"] --> G["7 Check before<br/>release"] --> H["8 Publish"]
    end
    B --> C
    E --> F

    classDef basics fill:#ffffff,stroke:#134a84,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000
    classDef writing fill:#134a84,stroke:#134a84,stroke-width:2px,color:#ffffff
    classDef finish fill:#f1a400,stroke:#f1a400,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000
    class A,B basics
    class C,D,E writing
    class F,G,H finish
```

If you are in a hurry: Chapter 1 gets you a running project, Chapter 7 is the
checklist, and Chapter 8 gets the course online. Everything in between is what
makes the course good.

## Try it now

Every chapter ends with questions like this one. Choose an answer and press
**Check answer**; the page tells you whether you were right and why. Nothing is
recorded anywhere, so guessing costs you nothing.

::: {.question}
In this template, what does one chapter correspond to?

- [ ] One line in the navigation file
- [x] One `.qmd` text file
- [ ] One folder of images
- [ ] One page in the Word document you started from

::: {.feedback}
Each chapter is a single `.qmd` file: plain text with a small amount of markup.
The navigation file only lists the chapters and puts them in order. Chapter 2
covers how the two fit together.
:::
:::

Some questions ask for a word instead. The tool that turns the text files into a
website is called [?]{.fitb answer="Quarto"} (type it in and click elsewhere).

## Before you start

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What you need

**R** and **RStudio**, both free. RStudio includes Quarto, the tool that builds
the website, so there is nothing else to install. You will not write or run any
R code: R is simply what RStudio runs on. A modern web browser is all a reader
needs.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Using this as your starting point

Chapter 1 explains exactly how to copy this project and turn it into your own
course. In short: duplicate the folder, replace the chapters, change a handful of
lines in one settings file.
:::
